requirements.requirement: Forward inventory-tagged log messages from node2 to a centralized collector on node1.
requirements.summary: Node2 was configured for persistent TCP forwarding to node1, both rsyslog configurations validated, and a tagged baseline message emitted on node2 was directly observed at node1.

requirements.requirement: Persist received inventory messages on node1 at /var/log/inventory/node2.log.
requirements.summary: The required file contained the forwarded baseline message, survived node1's restart, and subsequently accumulated fresh messages to 249 bytes.

requirements.requirement: Keep the logging flow working after node1 restarts.
requirements.summary: Node1 had a healthy pre-restart collector, acknowledged the scheduled restart, changed boot identity, recovered rsyslog, its TCP/514 listener, firewall state, and existing data, then received a fresh inventory message from node2.

requirements.requirement: Keep the logging flow working after node2 restarts.
requirements.summary: Node2 had a healthy pre-restart forwarder, acknowledged the scheduled restart, changed boot identity, returned to a fully running state with rsyslog active and enabled, and emitted a fresh message that was persisted on node1.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Direct end-to-end tests demonstrate forwarding to the exact required file, data persistence, and restored delivery after independent restarts of both managed nodes. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and corroborated by the fixed boot-identity snapshots.
limitations: The restart tests prove fresh delivery after each system recovered, but they did not explicitly emit a message while node1 was offline to exercise subsequent disk-queue replay.
The collector listener and firewall opening are broader than node2 alone; evidence does not describe the surrounding network-zone exposure.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had clear roles: creating the collector and forwarder configurations, opening the required collector port, restarting rsyslog, emitting bounded test records, and executing the mandatory restart protocol. No unnecessary troubleshooting mutation or retained residue was identified. Final snapshots show no failed services, healthy package state, and only the task-required TCP/514 listener added. Minor concern: TCP/514 was retained on all IPv4 and IPv6 interfaces rather than firewall-restricted specifically to node2, although the rsyslog ruleset filters accepted records by source address and program name.
